plan_seed: I climb the ladder, kneel, and rake the hay,
and check the apples in the slanting light,
in paper, each one wrapped and laid away.
The slates still hold the snow that fell last night.
Each week I come and see each cheek less red,
and hold them, feeling where the peel is thin.
One stain, one more. The blemishes have spread;
decay is moving deep below the skin.
I lift the spoiled apple, the knife in hand,
and pare away the bad. The blade goes deep.
These keep if hard and green. The ripe can't stand
the cold. I eat the ones no hands can keep.
I press the hay back where the bare boards show;
I lick my lips, and take the ladder slow.
